issue_context.title: Remove Net5CompatFileStreamStrategy in .NET 7 early previews
issue_context.body:
For .NET 6, we have made `FileStream` much faster and more reliable, thanks to an almost entire re-write. The rewrite has introduced [two breaking changes](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/file-io-improvements-in-dotnet-6/#breaking-changes). We assumed that it might have introduced bugs as well. Because of that, .NET 6 shipped with a built-in `FileStream` [.NET 5 compatibility mode](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/file-io-improvements-in-dotnet-6/#net-5-compatibility-mode) which users could request by using an app compat switch or an environment variable.

Our assumptions were right, the rewrite has introduced some edge-case bugs. All of the reported issues are already fixed:
* https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/61410 (backported to 6.0.1)
* https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/63625 (included in .NET 7 preview 1)

Since currently there are no known `FileStream` bugs introduced in .NET 6, the .NET 5 FileStream compatibility mode was [removed](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/57735). This change is included in .NET 7 preview 1.

Please let us know if there is any scenario that can’t be implemented in .NET 7 without using the .NET 5 compatibility mode.
